source_text: Qui etsi propter signum natus ex Virgine est, et tamen ita aversatus non est sexum virilem, ut eius susciperet veritatem, integer per omnia viscerum, integer corporis, homo verus, vir perfectus, si Petro apostolo creditur in Actibus disserenti [n86] ; intacta castitate conspicuus, et animum et oculos numquam remisso cordis vigore custodiens; sed quod hoc totum virtute mentis, non carnis infirmitate perfecerit, concupiscentiam carnis totius corporis immixtam sensibus, et veritatem ac sanitatem conditionemque membrorum fuisse in eo, et somnus eius, et cibus, et barba, et sudor, et labor, et crux testatur, et lancea. Non ergo sensus corporis non habuit ille, sed rexit. Hoc est unde Gentibus, unde Manichaeis insultat Catholicorum fides, quia verbum ut crucis, ita carnis eius, pereuntibus stultitia est, salvis autem futuris virtus Dei. Hoc est quod commendavit caritatem suam in nobis; quoniam quae lacerat impietas Manichaei, ea omnia pietas Mediatoris assumpsit. Nihil ergo me pudet in Domino meo; in quae propter salutem meam venit, teneo veritatem membrorum, ut exempli eius soliditatem arcemque suscipiam.
pass_a_gloss: Who although he was born from a Virgin on account of a sign, and nevertheless was not so averse to the male sex that he would not take up its truth, whole through all things of the viscera, whole of body, a true human being, a perfect man, if the apostle Peter is believed discussing in the Acts; conspicuous by untouched chastity, guarding both mind and eyes with never-slackened vigor of heart; but that he accomplished this whole by virtue of mind, not by infirmity of flesh, that the desire of the flesh mixed into the senses of the whole body, and the truth and health and condition of the members were in him, both his sleep, and food, and beard, and sweat, and labor, and the cross, and the lance testify. He therefore did not not have the senses of the body, but he ruled them. This is that from which the faith of the Catholics insults the Gentiles, insults the Manichaeans, because the word as of the cross, so of his flesh, is foolishness to those perishing, but to those about to be saved the power of God. This is what commended his charity in us; because all those things which the impiety of Manichaeus tears, the piety of the Mediator assumed. Nothing therefore shames me in my Lord; into which things he came on account of my salvation, I hold the truth of the members, that I may take up the solidity and citadel of his example.

pass_b_english: Although he was born from a virgin as a sign (compare Isaiah 7:14), he did not reject the male sex; rather, he assumed its reality. He was complete in every internal part, complete in body, a true human being, a perfect man, if we believe the apostle Peter’s discourse in Acts (Acts 2:22, 33). He was distinguished by unbroken chastity, guarding both mind and eyes without ever relaxing his heart’s strength. That he accomplished all this by strength of mind, not weakness of flesh, is witnessed by his sleep, food, beard, sweat, labor, cross, and the lance (compare Matthew 8:24; Luke 24:42–43; Isaiah 50:6; Luke 22:44; John 4:6; John 19:18, 34). These testify that the desire of the flesh, mingled with the senses of the whole body, and the reality, soundness, and natural condition of his members were present in him. He did not lack bodily sensations; he ruled them.

This is the ground on which the catholic faith challenges the nations and the Manichaeans: the message of his flesh, like that of his cross, is foolishness to those who perish, but God’s power to those who will be saved (compare 1 Corinthians 1:18). This is how he commended his love toward us (compare Romans 5:8): the Mediator’s devotion assumed everything that Manichaean impiety tears apart. Therefore nothing in my Lord makes me ashamed. I hold fast to the reality of the members he took on for my salvation, so that I may receive the solidity and strength of his example (Isaiah 7:14) (Matthew 8:24) (Luke 24:42–43) (Luke 22:44) (John 4:6) (John 19:18) (John 19:34) (1 Corinthians 1:18) (Romans 5:8).

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
